name: Nadi Shodhana · Anuloma Viloma
summary: Alternate-nostril breathing in Sivananda's 1:4:2 ratio: in through one side, a held breath gathered at the base of the spine, out through the other side. Beginners drop the hold (1:0:2).

steps.text: Sit upright. Right hand in Vishnu mudra: thumb for the right nostril, ring and little fingers for the left.
Close the right nostril and breathe in slowly through the left for 4 counts.
Close both nostrils and hold for 16 counts, resting attention at the base of the spine.
Open the right nostril and breathe out slowly for 8 counts.
Breathe in through the right for 4, hold for 16, breathe out through the left for 8. That is one round.
After the last round, rest in natural breath with attention between the eyebrows.

contraindications: Pregnancy: no breath retention; use the beginner (1:0:2) form.
High blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma or a recent eye/ear operation: no retention.
Never strain. If the next inhale is gasping, the hold was too long.

facets.needs_teacher_note: The 1:4:2 retention form is traditionally learned under a teacher; the 1:0:2 beginner form (Sivananda's Exercise No. 3) is safe to learn alone.

intro.caption: Sit tall. Right hand in Vishnu mudra. Let the breath settle.

round.caption: Close the right nostril. Breathe in through the left.
Close both. Hold gently, gathered at the base of the spine.
Release the thumb. Breathe out slowly through the right.
Breathe out slowly through the left.

outro.caption: Hand down. Breathe naturally. Rest between the eyebrows.

sources.cite: Swami Sivananda, The Science of Pranayama (DLS), ch. 3: 'Exercise No. 4' (left in 16 matras, hold 64, right out 32; begin with 1:4:2) and 'Exercise No. 3' (alternate nostril, no kumbhaka)
Same book, 'Pranayama for Awakening Kundalini': during the hold, send the current down the spine to the Muladhara (source of the 'held at the base' imagery)
Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres: Anuloma Viloma, ratio 1:4:2

meta.confidence_note: Ratio, nostril order and the no-kumbhaka beginner form are verified in the source. The visual of the hold gathering at the base comes from Sivananda's related Kundalini pranayama, not Sukha Purvaka itself (medium).
